propositions: git fetch of GitHub mirror intermittently hangs past 300s timeout due to missing http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime config, causing stalled byte-starved connections to burn full wall-clock budget instead of aborting on throughput
A connection that accepts but sends zero bytes should abort in seconds via throughput-keyed abort rather than the 300s ceiling
Legitimately slow but progressing fetches (e.g. 80 MB cold clone taking 90+ seconds) must not be aborted by the throughput floor
Low-speed abort failures should retry in-process a bounded number of times to self-heal transient stalls within a single review, while non-throughput failures like auth or bad refs should not retry
repo_snapshot.py at 788/800 LOC requires splitting git-subprocess and fetch-locking logic into new git_fetch.py module to stay within 800 LOC hard cap
